name: parses nested empty and singleton tuples canonically
unifies nested generic structures and substitutes return types
input: a generic tuple binding and reordered return
test:
actual = [parse_type('(int,str)'), 'bool']
patterns = [parse_type('(T,U)'), 'V']
result = infer_return_type(actual, patterns, parse_type('(V,U,T)'))
assert result == ('bool', 'str', 'int')
assert actual == [('int', 'str'), 'bool']
assert patterns == [('T', 'U'), 'V']

name: requires every repeated generic to have one compatible binding
input: same generic in separate and nested positions
test:
assert infer_return_type(["int", "int"], ["T", "T"], "T") == "int"
assert infer_return_type([("int", "str")], ["T"], "T") == ("int", "str")
for args in [
    (["int", "str"], ["T", "T"], "T"),
    ([("int",)], [("T", "U")], "T"),
    (["int"], ["T"], "U"),
    (["int"], ["T", "U"], "T"),
]:
    try:
        infer_return_type(*args)
    except (ValueError, AssertionError):
        pass
    else:
        assert False, args
